item.title: Cosmogenic isotopic evidence from Chang’e-6 clasts for excavation history and ejecta provenance in the South Pole-Aitken basin
item.dc:creator: Mi Zhou
Yingnan Zhang
Jian Chen
Ruixuan Luo
Ziwei Wang
Zhiwei Zuo
Deliang Chen
Kewei Chen
item.description:
Authors: Mi Zhou, Yingnan Zhang, Jian Chen, Ruixuan Luo, Ziwei Wang, Zhiwei Zuo, Deliang Chen, Kewei Chen, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Impact and space weathering play a key role in resurfacing the Moon, yet their effects on the lunar farside remain poorly constrained. Chang’e-6 (CE-6) samples provide a unique opportunity to understand space weathering and material redistributions within the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin. Our combined cosmogenic Sm, Hf, and Cr isotope results indicate an average cosmic-ray exposure (CRE) age of ~500 Ma for the CE-6 soil. Most low-Ti basaltic clasts experienced prolonged exposure similar to the host soil, whereas two were excavated more recently. Three KREEP-bearing clasts falling into two compositional groups show non-overlapping CRE ages, indicative of different excavation histories. Comparison with remote-sensing data suggests the Mg-rich pyroxene annulus and cryptomare as candidate source regions, respectively. These findings suggest that KREEP components are more widely distributed across the lunar farside than previously recognized.

item.title: Isolation of uranocenium, the bis-[8]annulene uranium cation
item.dc:creator: Cameron N. Deakin
Iulia Turcas
Benjamin L. L. Réant
Liam P. Griffin
John A. Seed
Adam Brookfield
David Collison
Eric J. L. McInnes
item.description:
Authors: Cameron N. Deakin, Iulia Turcas, Benjamin L. L. Réant, Liam P. Griffin, John A. Seed, Adam Brookfield, David Collison, Eric J. L. McInnes, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10914
Abstract: Abstract Uranocene, [U IV (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ], is the actinide equivalent to ferrocene. While ferrocene is readily oxidised to the ferrocenium cation, higher oxidation states of uranocene are unknown. Here we report the elusive uranocenium cation, [U V (η 8 -C 8 H 8 ) 2 ] + , and demonstrate using electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy and magnetometry that this formal U(V) complex has a 5 f 1 ground state. Enhanced uranium 5 f and 6 d mixing into filled δ-symmetry bonding orbitals in uranocenium, compared to uranocene, amplifies interorbital electron–electron repulsion, and counteracts bond length contraction, which minimises structural change. This manifests in solution where the uranocene/uranocenium redox couple exhibits near-ideal electrochemical reversibility, and in the solid-state where X-ray diffraction studies show minimal U–C bond length change upon oxidation. This demonstrates a case where actinide covalency governs molecular structure and physical properties across both solid and solution phases.

item.title: Marine primary production enhances removal of hydrophobic organic contaminants from Eurasian Arctic shelf waters
item.dc:creator: Xiaodi Shi
Laurent Oziel
Jonathan P. Benskin
Örjan Gustafsson
Anna Sobek
item.description:
Authors: Xiaodi Shi, Laurent Oziel, Jonathan P. Benskin, Örjan Gustafsson, Anna Sobek
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11074
Abstract: Abstract Global oceans store large quantities of human-made persistent hydrophobic organic contaminants (HOCs), driven by the organic carbon (OC) cycle. Despite diverse organic matter composition, bulk OC is typically treated as a uniform sorbent when assessing HOC fate. Significant uncertainty remains regarding the factors controlling variability in the sorption of HOCs by organic matter. Using surface sediments across the Eurasian Arctic shelves, spanning a land-to-ocean continuum of OC, we show that polychlorinated biphenyl concentrations per unit marine‑derived OC are up to an order of magnitude higher than those per unit terrestrial OC. Coupling these empirical relationships with a state‑of‑the‑art ocean biogeochemistry model shows that climate‑driven increases in marine primary production in the Eurasian Arctic shelves lead to 1.3 times more HOC removal from the water column. These findings reveal that both OC quantity and quality control the sediment HOC sink and that climate‑induced shifts in OC cycles may restructure HOC fate in the Arctic Ocean.

item.title: High-numerical-aperture extreme ultraviolet flat optics via a cascaded momentum relay
item.dc:creator: Xiaoqi Jiang
Maoxiong Zhao
Shaohua Yang
Lan Lan
Chao Song
Fang Wu
Yang Bu
item.description:
Authors: Xiaoqi Jiang, Maoxiong Zhao, Shaohua Yang, Lan Lan, Chao Song, Fang Wu, Yang Bu
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract High-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet flat optics are constrained by undersampling of steep edge phase gradients, which reduces phase fidelity and high-angle diffraction efficiency. Here, we introduce a momentum-relay architecture that partitions large wavevector deflections across two cascaded elements. A 4:1 demagnification platform operating at 532 nm synthesizes an effective numerical aperture of 0.80, producing a measured first-dark-ring radius of 413.2 nm and resolving ~555 nm image-plane features across a 100 μm-diameter field of view. We further translate the concept to 13.24 nm using a compact xenon laser-produced-plasma source. Two Fresnel zone plates, each with a numerical aperture of approximately 0.33, cooperatively synthesize an effective numerical aperture of approximately 0.53. Here, we show that cascaded momentum relay provides a compact route to high-numerical-aperture extreme-ultraviolet projection while relaxing the feature-size and spatial-sampling requirements imposed on each element.

item.title: A global livestock virome catalog links viruses with resistome assembly
item.dc:creator: Lan Jiang
Bintao Li
Liusheng Lei
Zishu Liu
Wei Sun
Liping Ma
Chang-Jun Cha
Timothy Johnson
item.description:
Authors: Lan Jiang, Bintao Li, Liusheng Lei, Zishu Liu, Wei Sun, Liping Ma, Chang-Jun Cha, Timothy Johnson, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Livestock manure is a prominent One Health setting for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the contribution of viruses to resistome assembly remains unresolved. Here we compile the Livestock Manure Virus Database (LMVD), a global catalog of 1,330,372 viral operational taxonomic units reconstructed from 4,017 metagenomes. Livestock manure viral communities exhibit restricted biogeographic distributions, and antibiotic use and farming scale show the highest relative predictive importance for viral diversity. Viral genomes contained 78 antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) subtypes, representing 9.1% of resistome diversity in livestock manure, but virus-encoded ARGs were infrequent. Bacteriophages instead showed extensive predicted links to bacterial hosts, with nearly all antibiotic-resistant bacteria linked to viruses, predominantly temperate viruses, and enrichment in pathogenic antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Together, these findings place bounds on the contribution of viruses to direct ARG dissemination and indicate that lysogenic interactions with resistant hosts may shape AMR risk.

item.title: Global-scale variability of glacier velocity and mass loss across terminus environments
item.dc:creator: Joseph Mallalieu
Jonathan L. Carrivick
Matthias Huss
Iestyn D. Barr
Nicholas E. Barrand
Cassandra L. Raby
item.description:
Authors: Joseph Mallalieu, Jonathan L. Carrivick, Matthias Huss, Iestyn D. Barr, Nicholas E. Barrand, Cassandra L. Raby
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10873
Abstract: Abstract The environment in which a glacier terminates can strongly influence its behaviour, stability and future evolution, yet the relationship between terminus type and glacier dynamics at the global scale remains poorly constrained. Here we present a globally-complete classification of glacier termini distinguishing between land, lake, marine and shelf environments, and integrate it with datasets of glacier geometry, dynamics and climate. We show that although lake-, marine- and shelf-terminating glaciers comprise only 3.2% of glaciers globally, they account for over half of global glacier area and mass loss. We also show that lake- and marine-terminating glaciers flow, on average, 10% and 44% faster than land-terminating glaciers, respectively. Furthermore, specific (area-normalised) mass loss rates at lake-terminating glaciers are 57% greater than those at land- and marine-terminating glaciers. Our findings underscore the need for improved representation of non-land glacier termini in models of glacier evolution and sea-level rise, and suggest that distinguishing the environmental and geometric controls of termini on glacier dynamics remains an important challenge for future research.

item.title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis
item.dc:creator: David Jorgensen
Noémie Lefrancq
Nicholas C. Grassly
Louis du Plessis
Margarita Pons-Salort
item.description:
Authors: David Jorgensen, Noémie Lefrancq, Nicholas C. Grassly, Louis du Plessis, Margarita Pons-Salort
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

item.title: Ultrafast single-qubit gates through multi-photon transition removal
item.dc:creator: Y. Gao
A. Galicia
J. D. Da Costa Jesus
Y. Liu
Y. Haddad
D. A. Volkov
J. R. Guimarães
H. Bhardwaj
item.description:
Authors: Y. Gao, A. Galicia, J. D. Da Costa Jesus, Y. Liu, Y. Haddad, D. A. Volkov, J. R. Guimarães, H. Bhardwaj, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10874
Abstract: Abstract Fast qubit control is essential for scalable quantum computing. However, the strong driving that is required can induce significant leakage from the computational subspace, particularly in weakly anharmonic qubits. We demonstrate single qubit gates with a total leakage error consistently below 2.0 × 10 −5 on a transmon qubit, and obtain fidelities above 99.98% at 6.8 ns pulse duration in both X and X /2 gates. This is achieved by removing direct transitions beyond nearest-neighbor levels using double recursive applications of Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate pulse shape. We also introduce the amplified leakage error sequence which can directly measure the leakage error down to 10 −6 . We test single qubit gates across a range of pulse durations using multiple benchmarking methods to reveal the error channels. The presented approach can be straightforwardly adapted by other platforms.

item.title: Force-driven single-molecule transformations through tip-mediated stabilization of transition states
item.dc:creator: Kota Iwata
Ikutaro Hamada
Ranmaru Kuno
Taku Enomoto
Ryu Kuroki
Hidehiro Sakurai
Yoshiaki Sugimoto
item.description:
Authors: Kota Iwata, Ikutaro Hamada, Ranmaru Kuno, Taku Enomoto, Ryu Kuroki, Hidehiro Sakurai, Yoshiaki Sugimoto
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10868
Abstract: Abstract Mechanochemistry uses mechanical forces to drive chemical transformations, offering an energy-efficient alternative to traditional thermal, optical, or electrical reaction pathways. At the single-molecule scale, controlling structural changes with mechanical stimuli is fundamental for developing nanoscale devices and understanding chemical reactivity. In conventional single-molecule reactions driven by light or electrical currents, energy is supplied through one-way excitation processes, requiring the single-event energy input to exceed the activation energy barrier. Here we show that mechanically driven single-molecule reactions can bypass this limitation, proceeding with a net energy cost below the activation energy. By using atomic force microscopy to induce the structural inversion of individual, bowl-shaped sumanene molecules on a gold surface, we measure the mechanical energy spent during the transformation. The net energy cost is significantly lower than the theoretical activation energy. This sub-barrier reaction occurs because attractive van der Waals forces from the mesoscopic tip body stabilize the transition state more effectively than the final state. Our findings demonstrate a distinct energetic mechanism in mechanochemistry, highlighting alternative strategies for energy-efficient molecular manipulation.

item.title: Tom70–mediated mitochondria–nuclear envelope contacts regulate nuclear pore complex inheritance during gametogenesis
item.dc:creator: Cyrus T. Ruediger
Benjamin S. Styler
Eric M. Sawyer
Silvan Spiri
Grant A. King
Madison E. Walsh
Gloria A. Brar
Danielle M. Jorgens
item.description:
Authors: Cyrus T. Ruediger, Benjamin S. Styler, Eric M. Sawyer, Silvan Spiri, Grant A. King, Madison E. Walsh, Gloria A. Brar, Danielle M. Jorgens, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Gametogenesis rejuvenates the cellular lineage and excludes senescence-associated factors from gametes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae , this involves sequestration of nuclear constituents into the Gametogenesis Uninherited Nuclear Compartment (GUNC), which is excluded from gametes. Here we identify the conserved mitochondrial import receptor Tom70 as a key regulator of GUNC-mediated exclusion. Loss of TOM70 disrupts the sequestration of nuclear pore complexes, but not senescence-associated aggregates and nucleolar components, into the GUNC. Tom70’s role appears independent of its canonical function in mitochondrial import and instead reflects a meiosis-specific requirement for mitochondria-nuclear envelope tethering. During meiosis II, Tom70 concentrates around the GUNC, where it recruits the nuclear envelope tethering protein Cnm1. Loss of CNM1 partially phenocopies tom70 ∆, consistent with parallel tethering interactions. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized organelle contact-dependent pathway that remodels the nuclear envelope to support selective nuclear inheritance. More broadly, they highlight how organelle contacts integrate with nuclear quality control to safeguard gamete integrity.

item.title: Giant orbital Zeeman effects in a magnetic topological van der Waals interphase
item.dc:creator: Tobias Wichmann
Mirco Sastges
Keda Jin
Jose Martinez-Castro
Tom G. Saunderson
Dongwook Go
Honey Boban
Samir Lounis
item.description:
Authors: Tobias Wichmann, Mirco Sastges, Keda Jin, Jose Martinez-Castro, Tom G. Saunderson, Dongwook Go, Honey Boban, Samir Lounis, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11076
Abstract: Abstract Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures allow the engineering of magnetic and electronic properties via interfacial orbital hybridization and charge transfer. The resulting electric fields can give rise to Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, which may stabilize novel two-dimensional magnetic phases. While such emergent magnetic ‘interphases’ may offer a promising platform for spin-based electronics, direct spectroscopic evidence for them is still lacking. Here, we report electric-field tunable Zeeman effects with Landé g -factors up to ≈ 230 at the interface of graphene and the vdW ferromagnet Fe 3 GeTe 2 . They arise from an interplay of local-moment canting and the itinerant orbital moments of Fe 3 GeTe 2 , producing a giant asymmetric level splitting. Exploiting the inelastic phonon gap of graphene, scanning tunneling spectroscopy allows us to access the buried interface properties, and quantify Faraday-like screening. Our findings provide new insights and opportunities for electrically controlled interface magnetism, e.g. for spintronics and orbitronics devices.

item.title: Unveiling the functional specialisation of human white matter circuits with naturalistic stimuli
item.dc:creator: M. Ovando-Tellez
C. Foulon
V. Nozais
V. Pacella
M. Thiebaut de Schotten
item.description:
Authors: M. Ovando-Tellez, C. Foulon, V. Nozais, V. Pacella, M. Thiebaut de Schotten
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Functional MRI (fMRI) has traditionally focused on grey matter activations, overlooking the contribution of white matter pathways to brain organisation. Yet evidence suggests that white matter constrains, modulates, and integrates signals across distant regions. Here, we introduce a framework to map the functional specialisation of white matter circuits using fMRI scans collected while participants watched naturalistic videos. By leveraging ecologically valid stimuli, this method captures cognition as it naturally unfolds. Integrating fMRI with brain connections, we derived a functionally grounded parcellation of the connectome, challenging conventional cortical-based cognitive taxonomy. Distinct cognitive profiles emerged for association and commissural fibres, with association pathways preferentially linked to language-related processes and commissural pathways to executive and motor functions, affirming the functionally heterogeneous nature of white matter systems. An artificial intelligence framework applied to independent datasets confirmed the robustness and functional relevance of the identified parcels. This open-access framework also enables the interactive exploration of white matter functional organisation, offering a new lens on the neural bases of cognition.

item.title: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
item.dc:creator: Samir Abu-Rumeileh
Henning Großkopf
Arthur Guthknecht
Alexander Mensch
Dirk Osterloh
Antonia Ratti
Julian Conrad
Caroline Stapf
item.description:
Authors: Samir Abu-Rumeileh, Henning Großkopf, Arthur Guthknecht, Alexander Mensch, Dirk Osterloh, Antonia Ratti, Julian Conrad, Caroline Stapf, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10745
Abstract: Abstract Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS ( n = 139), AD ( n = 101) and controls ( n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain ( n = 16), spinal cord ( n = 11) and muscle ( n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. Mass spectrometry revealed a central-to-peripheral shift from BD-tau to big tau predominance, with exclusively big p-tau217 detected in muscle. Selective detection of BD-tau species improves the specificity of blood AD biomarkers by reducing peripheral tau confounding.

item.title: Long-term electoral participation among Swedish survivors of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
item.dc:creator: Kalle Ekholm
Lina M. Eriksson
Kåre Vernby
item.description:
Authors: Kalle Ekholm, Lina M. Eriksson, Kåre Vernby
Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 11038
Abstract: Abstract Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data ( N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government’s crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.

item.title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
item.dc:creator: Junghyun Lim
Marijana Vujkovic
Michael G. Levin
Kim Lorenz
Benjamin F. Voight
David Y. Zhang
Max. F. Dudek
Matthew C. Pahl
item.description:
Authors: Junghyun Lim, Marijana Vujkovic, Michael G. Levin, Kim Lorenz, Benjamin F. Voight, David Y. Zhang, Max. F. Dudek, Matthew C. Pahl, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Gallstone disease is a highly prevalent and costly gastrointestinal disease. Yet, genetic variation in gallstone susceptibility and its implication in metabolic pathways remain to be explored. We report a trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease including 100,856 cases and 1,596,602 controls in the UK Biobank, FinnGen, Biobank Japan, and Million Veteran Program. We identified 116 (59 novel) risk loci across meta-analysis and found replication in statistically compelling signals in the All of Us Research Program. A polygenic risk score constructed from trans-ancestry lead variants was positively associated with liver chemistry and alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency and negatively associated with total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein levels among trans-ancestry and European ancestry groups in the Penn Medicine BioBank. Colocalization of risk loci with 44 traits and with expression quantitative trait loci from eight tissues yielded 321 and 110 significant colocalizations, respectively. These findings broaden our understanding of the genetic architecture of gallstone disease.

Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10446
Abstract: Abstract Multi-Tb/s optical interconnects for artificial intelligence data centers necessitate high-speed, energy-efficient, and compact transceivers. However, conventional silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators are fundamentally limited by low modulation efficiency and large physical dimensions that typically extend several millimeters, requiring high-swing drivers and power-intensive digital signal processing to achieve data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s per lane. Here we show a silicon photonic crystal waveguide slow-light modulator that overcomes the bandwidth-efficiency trade-off via a built-in electro-optic equalizer. By monolithically integrating optical delay lines and crossings within segmented slow-light phase shifters, we synthesized an on-chip feedforward response that extends the 3-dB bandwidth. The fabricated modulator with a small device length of 320 µm demonstrated 140-Gb/s on-off keying operation with an energy consumption of 26 fJ/bit using drive voltages compatible with fin field-effect transistor-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology. Furthermore, four-level pulse amplitude modulation achieved 180 Gb/s without digital signal processing and 200 Gb/s with a low-complexity 11-tap digital equalizer. By reducing reliance on power-dissipating electronics, this strategy provides a potential route toward future dense multi-Tb/s co-packaged optics for energy-constrained switching systems.

item.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing

Authors: E. Mayner, Y. Zhumagulov, C. de Giorgio, F. Chu, P. P. Swain, G. E. Fantner, A. Kis, O. V. Yazyev, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are promising platforms for quantum information technologies and nanoscale sensing. The negatively charged boron vacancy ( $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − ) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is particularly attractive due to its sensitivity to temperature, magnetic fields, and pressure, but its application is limited by intrinsically weak photoluminescence (PL). Here we demonstrate a van der Waals heterostructure that enhances the PL intensity of $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − by up to 45× at 4 Kelvin while preserving compatibility with ultrathin optoelectronic platforms. A quasi type-I band alignment at the PbI 2 –defected hBN interface facilitates efficient interlayer coupling to the defect, and strong spectral overlap supports fluorescence resonance energy transfer. Ab initio calculations indicate that this coupling enables a photon-ratcheting mechanism, in which optical absorption in PbI 2 generates a nonlinear polarization that drives $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − excitation. This process is compatible with interlayer energy transfer while maintaining minimal electronic and spin hybridization and preserving optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The heterostructure further exhibits improved sensitivity to external magnetic fields. These results establish a route for the enhancement of defect emission via interlayer optical coupling and introduce a general materials strategy for amplifying weak quantum defect signals in nanomaterials.

Abstract: Abstract Insect-scale flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles offer substantial potential for applications such as search and rescue. However, stringent power and payload constraints at the sub-gram scale have precluded sustained untethered flight. Inspired by the high lift generated by full-circumferential rotor motion, this study presents a cross-shaped piezoelectric direct-drive V-wing structure. The structure uses a tuning-fork vibration mode to generate full-circumferential flapping, suppressing fuselage vibration without external anchoring and substantially improving the lift performance of the piezoelectric direct-drive flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. Based on this principle, we developed a cross-shaped four-piezoelectric-actuator V-wing micro aerial vehicle weighing 389 mg with a wingspan of 6.8 cm, capable of generating a maximum lift of 1850 mg. Waveform modulation increases the efficiency of the 173 mg drive circuit to 45%, while mechanical self-stabilization suppresses attitude disturbances. Integrated with a 350 mg battery, the 984 mg system achieves untethered, sustained, stable flight for a sub-gram flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. The maximum lift-to-weight ratio of the untethered flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle system is 1.88. Its maximum flight altitude exceeds 10 m, and its continuous flight duration under low-power operation exceeds 240 s. The system also demonstrates altitude-controlled and disturbance-resilient untethered flight.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) short-wave infrared (SWIR) detectors (1-2 µm) are of great interest for a plethora of applications including autonomous driving, machine vision, night and adverse weather imaging, in view of their low-cost and compatibility to read-out electronics. However, to date, CQDs photodetectors still suffer from high dark current and thereby noise such that their performance remains inferior to epitaxially grown III-V semiconductors. This performance gap originates from the limited passivation of non-polar surfaces existent in large PbS CQDs needed to access the SWIR spectral range. Here we report on a lead-thiolate based chemistry that serves to passivate both polar and non-polar surfaces of PbS CQDs yielding inks with unprecedented optoelectronic quality evidenced by open circuit voltage deficit and dark current activation energies matching those of single crystalline semiconductors. As a result, we demonstrate infrared photodetectors with remarkable thermal resilience, very low dark current density ( ~ 34 nA cm −2 at −1 V) and a specific detectivity D* of ~8×10 12 Jones. The measured D* value is on par with that of commercially available InGaAs photodiodes (PDs).

item.title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair

item.description:
Authors: Stefan Braunshier, Elda Cannavo, Vincent Morin, Sriram KK, Ananya Acharya, Giordano Reginato, Florian Morati, Virginie Ropars, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired by Ku-dependent non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) or DNA end resection-dependent homologous recombination (HR). Previously, it was shown that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 can remove Ku from DSBs and initiate resection, showing flexibility in DSB repair pathway choice. However, which NHEJ intermediates can be disrupted by resection factors remains unknown. Using reconstituted reactions with purified S. cerevisiae proteins, we show here that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 is not directly inhibited by any of the core NHEJ factors. Instead, we find that MRX-pSae2 is inhibited structurally. DNA synapsis, a dynamic NHEJ intermediate that bridges DSBs, strongly suppresses resection. Non-ligatable ends are refractory to MRX-pSae2 once synapsis formed, and NHEJ assemblies with catalytic mutants of DNA ligase IV that permit synapsis but do not allow ligation likewise inhibit resection. We further demonstrate that removal of Ku from DSBs requires RPA, which interacts with MRX and pSae2 to synergistically stimulate MRX 3′−5′ exonuclease activity, generating free 3′ overhangs. Our data support a model in which DNA synapsis temporarily prevents resection, allowing NHEJ to execute ligation. If ligation fails and synapsis dissociates, MRX-pSae2 and RPA promote resection that removes non-productive NHEJ assemblies and channels DSB repair toward HR. The data help explain the suppression of NHEJ by RPA observed in previous genetic experiments.

Abstract: Abstract While magnetometers based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond have emerged as the most important solid-state quantum sensors, ensembles are typically limited to a few percent optical contrast. By integrating the NV centers into a laser cavity, we show magnetic-field-dependent shifts of the laser threshold, allowing the laser system to be entirely switched off with the NV centers’ magnetic resonance. We determine the photon-shot-noise fundamental sensitivity limit to be < 400 fT/ $$\sqrt{{{\rm{Hz}}}}$$ Hz for all vector components and demonstrate that it improves super-linearly with contrast. This sensitivity is not achieved at the usual cost of smaller linewidth, i.e., maintains good intrinsic dynamic range. This provides a perspective for highly sensitive magnetometry operated outside magnetically-shielded rooms for applications including magnetoencephalography, magnetic navigation, and magnetic anomaly detection.

Abstract: Abstract X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is essential for extraembryonic tissue growth and embryo development in mice. However, species-specific differences in its timing and regulation have left its role in human development unclear. Here, we show that the in vitro differentiation of naive human pluripotent stem cells to trophoblast stem cells and extraembryonic mesoderm cells is accompanied by XCI. Furthermore, we show that XCI is needed for the survival of human female extraembryonic cells. Together, these findings link XCI to the formation of human extraembryonic lineages, with important implications for human reproductive biology.

item.dc:creator: Ashley J. Newton

Authors: Ashley J. Newton, Adefoluke E. Kuforiji, Philipp A. M. Schmidpeter
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Cell membranes are not only protective barriers but also active chemical environments that regulate protein structure and function. However, how individual lipid species influence membrane proteins across physiological concentration ranges, either as specific ligands or through bilayer-mediated solvent effects, remains poorly defined. Here, using the cyclic nucleotide-gated ion channel SthK reconstituted into defined membranes, we show that phosphatidic acid enhances channel activity across all tested concentrations but, at low mole fractions ( ~ 0.7-1 mol%), it selectively and cooperatively increases agonist potency, meeting criteria for a site‑specific allosteric ligand. In contrast, the zwitterionic lipid phosphatidylethanolamine modulates SthK activity exclusively through linear, solvent‑like effects across the same concentration range. Structural analysis reveals that low anionic lipid content expands the closed‑state conformational ensemble without promoting pore opening, providing a structural basis for lipid-dependent latent allostery. Together, these results establish lipid concentration as a governing regulatory variable that quantitatively distinguishes ligand‑like from solvent‑like mechanisms of membrane protein regulation.

Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10790
Abstract: Abstract Cell Painting is a popular high-content imaging assay that captures the shape and internal organization of 2D cell cultures at scale. While 3D cell cultures are more physiologically relevant models – especially for studying drug perturbations – they remain challenging to image because light scatters before it reaches the cultures’ interior. We show that tissue-clearing, a technique that makes spheroids transparent, combined with a focusing routine that locates spheroids on the fly, enables Cell Painting at single-cell level inside intact spheroids. Notably, the effect of two drugs, 5-fluorouracil and olaparib, nearly indistinguishable in 2D monolayers, diverged in spheroids. This finding was then corroborated by DNA-damage, cell-cycle, and gene-expression assays. The workflow runs on a spinning-disk confocal microscope in a standard 384-well plate format, making single-cell 3D profiling accessible to laboratories already performing Cell Painting.

Abstract: Abstract The transcription factor TFE3 coordinates cellular adaptation to stress. While its acute activation is cytoprotective, chronic TFE3 dysregulation is linked to diverse pathologies. Here, we characterize the cellular landscape of TFE3-NDD, a recently described neurodevelopmental disorder caused by mutations that disrupt the TFE3-Rag GTPase interface, leading to constitutive TFE3 nuclear localization. Using patient-derived fibroblasts, we show that TFE3-NDD is primarily a metabolic and homeostatic disorder. Mutant cells undergo a profound rewiring toward oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), resulting in metabolic rigidity and a vulnerability to energy failure. Despite a massive expansion of the lysosomal compartment, we observe a paradoxical qualitative failure characterized by impaired acidification, defective protease maturation, increased lysosomal exocytosis, and aberrant cathepsin K secretion. This secretory phenotype is coupled with a destabilized cell-extracellular matrix interface, marked by impaired migration, defective coordination between actomyosin tension and focal adhesion maturation, and a loss of synaptic stabilizers. Notably, TFE3-NDD shares a signature of high OXPHOS and ferroptosis resistance with TFE3-dependent cancers, such as translocation renal cell carcinoma. Our findings reveal how the chronic hyperactivation of a protective stress-response factor collapses cellular homeostasis, providing a mechanistic framework for the tissue malformations and neurodevelopmental deficits that define TFE3-NDD.

Abstract: Abstract The gut microbiome in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is enriched in proinflammatory bacteria, yet defining a consistent dysbiotic signature is challenging, due to substantial variation between individuals and over time. IBD-associated bacteria showed reduced persistence within hosts, increased strain loss and diminished strain engraftment. 8% of commensal species displayed strain-level associations with IBD that were independent of species-level changes, suggesting distinct ecological strategies for persistence. Finally, defining an inflammatory index, we demonstrated that inflammation explains much of the observed variation in microbial composition and abundance. Together, our findings indicate that inflammation associates and likely contributes to loss of commensals, thereby limiting microbiome recovery and resilience.

Abstract: Abstract Graphene nanoscrolls (GNSs), one-dimensional nanostructures formed by rolling up a single sheet of graphene, exhibit electronic and mechanical properties distinct from the original graphene sheet. This method also allows control of the scroll angle, i.e., chiral angle, by controlling the stretch direction of the tape/graphene stack. The nanoscroll structure allows the intercalation of metal chloride molecules, resulting in an increase of the electrical conductivity. Furthermore, heteronanoscrolls of graphene and MoS 2 are realized by stretching MoS 2 /graphene heterostacks, exhibiting clear optical response. Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Since their rapid adoption from the mid 2000s, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) have been one of the most impactful malaria interventions in Africa. Facing insecticide resistance and ever-increasing resource constraints, there is a growing need to revise previous modelling efforts of ITN coverage to better reflect the current epidemiological reality. Comprehensive estimates of ITN coverage must account for factors such as net type, net age, and user behaviours. By leveraging improved data availability, we propose a mathematically rigorous ITN coverage model that extends previous national-level models to the subnational level across 44 countries in Africa. The presented Multitype-ITN (MITN) model is used to construct longitudinal estimates of net demography by age and type from 2006-2024, and provide insights on potential sources of ITN distribution inefficiencies. Our findings show a significant increase in the uptake of next-generation ITNs, reflecting an increasingly diverse market. However, longitudinal trends suggests stagnation in key metrics of net coverage (nets-per-capita, access and use), alongside a downwards trend in utilisation – number of users per net, coupled with observed stationary use rates – proportion of people with access that also use nets. There are also early signs of interventions failing to meet the demands of increasing populations.

Abstract: Abstract The organization of signaling proteins into multi-component complexes is essential for innate immune responses and is often achieved through the oligomerization of death domains (DDs). The Myddosome, composed of MyD88 and IRAK family kinases, exemplifies this mechanism. However, how DDs assemble in an ordered and regulated manner to form Myddosomes to control signaling output remains unclear. Here, we show that IRAK4 kinase activity and autophosphorylation are required for IRAK4:IRAK1 heterotypic DD interactions. We show that IRAK1 is autoinhibited by its kinase domain, and IRAK4 phosphorylation relieves this inhibition, enabling IRAK1 DD incorporation into Myddosomes. This phosphorylation-dependent switch similarly controls IRAK2/3 incorporation. Thus, IRAK4 autophosphorylation acts as an energy-dependent molecular switch that integrates phosphorylation with protein oligomerization to drive Myddosome maturation and signal transduction. This mechanism demonstrates how enzymatic activity can impose temporal and spatial control over macromolecular assembly to ensure directional and context-dependent inflammatory signaling.

Abstract: Abstract Paclitaxel is a highly valuable diterpenoid anticancer drug originally extracted from the yew tree. Due to the low efficiency of plant extraction and the high cost of semi-synthesis, efforts have been made to produce paclitaxel through biosynthesis. However, there have been no reports to date on engineered strains capable of paclitaxel biosynthesis. Here, we engineer a paclitaxel-producing line using the moss ( Physcomitrium patens ) chassis cells by combining transient expression verification, cytoplasmic localization strategies, self-cleaving 2 A peptide-mediated multi-gene co-expression systems and a modular iterative transformation strategy for stable genetic inheritance. Journal: Nature Communications; Volume: 17; Issue: 1; Article number: 10693
Abstract: Abstract Mortality rates for African children with severe malaria remain high. Sevuparin, a heparin-like compound, as an adjunctive treatment, may improve outcomes due to its effects on Plasmodium falciparum -infected erythrocytes. A Phase I dose-finding trial in Kenyan and Zambian children with severe malaria aimed to identify the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of sevuparin, given as three infusions (at 0, 8 and 16 h post-enrolment) using the continual reassessment method (ISRCTN32271864). The primary endpoint was dose limiting toxicity (DLT) defined as Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time (APTT) > 95 seconds (2.5x upper limit of normal) across 1.5-6 mg/kg doses. Secondary endpoints were lactate clearance, parasite half-life, APTT at 24 h and grade 3-4 serious adverse events. Twenty-three children were enroled; 20 were included in the primary analysis, across 10 cohorts. A data monitoring committee followed model recommendations, leading to dose escalation from 1.5 mg/kg through all doses to 6 mg/kg when 2 DLTs occurred. During de-escalation, DLTs occurred at 5 mg/kg and 4 mg/kg. The final dose was therefore 3 mg/kg. There was 1 death (1/23 (4.3%)), 1 readmission and 1 grade 3 non-DLT adverse event: all judged unrelated to sevuparin. MTD of 3 mg/kg sevuparin in each of three infusions at 0, 8 and 16 h was identified for future investigation.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Histone proteins package DNA into nucleosomes, forming chromatin and thereby safeguarding genome integrity. Proper histone expression is essential for cell proliferation and chromatin organization, yet the upstream regulators of histone supply remain incompletely understood. PRMT5, a protein arginine methyltransferase that catalyzes symmetric dimethylation of arginine residues, is frequently overexpressed in cancer and targeted in multiple clinical trials, but its cell-essential function remains unclear. Using time-resolved nascent transcriptional profiling, quantitative proteomics, and imaging, we show that PRMT5 activity is required to sustain histone transcription and histone protein synthesis during S phase. PRMT5 inhibition or knockdown leads to rapid, p53-independent depletion of histone mRNA, leading to loss of histone proteins and accumulation of replication-associated nuclear abnormalities. Parallel depletion of the histone gene transcription factor HINFP produces similar genomic instability, linking defective histone production to loss of genome integrity. We further show that histone H4 accumulates at both histone genes and histone locus bodies (HLBs) and that H4R3me2s is enriched at HLBs. These findings support a model in which PRMT5-mediated methylation of histone H4 regulates histone transcription. Our findings establish PRMT5 as a central coordinator of histone homeostasis and provide a mechanistic rationale for its essential role in proliferating cells.

Authors: Renjie Liao, Defeng Fu, Zaoxu Xu, Han Liang, Xiaoran Zhou, Yiling Chen, Xueqi Liu, Jiajun Cheng, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. In the last couple of years, the spatial resolution for the capture addresses has been improved from ~100 μm to <1 μm, well below the size of a mammalian cell. However, the capture efficiency of sequencing-based methods is generally low, which diminishes the effect of high capture resolution and negatively impacts subsequent data interpretation. Here, we introduce a spatial transcriptomic system, which provides ~1 μm capture resolution and a much higher capture efficiency. We demonstrate that as high as ~14,000 UMIs can be captured from mouse testis sample per 10 × 10 μm² area at a sequencing saturation of 0.43. Rare cells organized in single-cell-layers can be recovered when the data was analyzed at an effective resolution of 2 μm.

Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Electrocatalytic urea synthesis from CO 2 and NO 3 – offers a sustainable alternative to energy-intensive industrial methods, yet precise C–N coupling remains hindered by kinetic mismatches between the reduction reactions. Here, we report a strategy leveraging programmable Zn-node gasification to thermally sculpt 1.5–1.8 nm cavities within zeolitic imidazolate frameworks, hosting atomically dispersed Cu–N 4 sites. An optimal confinement metric descriptor (9.64) is introduced as a predictive parameter, correlating cavity geometry with local electric-field and Cu d-band modulation. This design stabilizes *CO and *NO intermediates, effectively suppressing parasitic reactions and lowering C–N coupling barriers. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a urea yield of 71.32 g g cat –1 h –1 with 98.9% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in gas diffusion cells. Pilot-scale testing demonstrates stable operation over 300 h with an FE of 90%, establishing nanoconfinement as a design principle for competitive-performance urea electrosynthesis.

Abstract: Abstract Protein synthesis depends on specialized regulatory factors to overcome difficult-to-translate sequences during elongation that cause ribosomal stalling. In human mitochondria, this function is carried out by TACO1 (Translation activator of COX1). Unlike the prokaryotic elongation factor EF-P and the eukaryotic eIF5A, which bind the ribosomal E site and stabilize P-site tRNA to facilitate peptide bond formation, TACO1 adopts a distinct strategy. Using AlphaFold analysis and molecular dynamics simulations, we further show how a series of conformational changes allow its N-terminal domain to reorient and transiently engage with the A-site tRNA via a conserved and functionally critical basic amino acid patch. The bacterial homolog of TACO1, namely YebC2, shares the structural features required for its function. Overall, we present an evolutionarily conserved mechanism employed by TACO1 to enhance mitochondrial translation efficiency.

Abstract: Abstract Inflammation resolution depends on coordinated communication between tissue compartments, yet how the intestinal epithelium shapes its immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, using colonic biopsies from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and mouse models enabling tissue-wide visualization of NF-κB activity, we combine single-cell RNA sequencing and secretome analysis to define epithelial communication during colitis. Thus, we identify dynamic epithelial–immune communication and demonstrate a protective IEC NF-κB–Treg cell axis important for resolution of intestinal inflammation.

Abstract: Abstract Humans and animals are ubiquitously colonized by Enterobacteriaceae , including both commensals and clinically significant pathogens. The plasmids encode multi-drug efflux systems and potential secreted effectors. Up to 208 tRNAs are encoded and include sequence variants that may counter tRNA-centric defense mechanisms. Abstract: Abstract Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

Abstract: Abstract Detailed photophysical measurements of the non-symmetric heptazine, HzTFEX 2 , previously reported as having inverted S 1 -T 1 levels, show complex behaviour, highly dependent on environment, concentration and aggregation. However, by exciting S 0 →S 2 at 77 K, we observe a consistent phosphorescence signal at 425 nm, 110 ± 20 meV above the S 0 ←S 1 emission, whereas exciting S 0 →S 1 does not give phosphorescence or delayed fluorescence (DF). We conclude that coupling between S 2 and S 1 is very weak, S 2 -T N intersystem crossing is effective, whereas S 1 ↔T 1 intersystem crossing is thermally activated, fulfilling the conditions required for the observation of inverted phosphorescence. At room temperature, no long-lived DF is observed because exothermic T 1 →S 1 ISC becomes allowed, such that in an OLED, high efficiency can be achieved.

item.title: Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
item.dc:creator: N. Kida
T. Togashi
K. Tono
Y. Ikemoto
K. Sawada
item.description:
Authors: N. Kida, T. Togashi, K. Tono, Y. Ikemoto, K. Sawada
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Here, we report the first observation of terahertz emission induced by hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses in solids, providing evidence for X-ray DFG. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. These results establish XFEL-induced terahertz emission as a general platform for probing second-order X-ray nonlinearities and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

item.description:
Authors: Sofia Micheli, Adrian Salas-Bastos, Khanh Huỳnh, Virginia Cecconi, Isabel Kolm, Jelena Vasilevska, Julien Debbache, Peter F. Renz, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Although tumor innervation is known to promote cancer progression, underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood and have mostly been linked to axonal signaling. Here, we identify peripheral glia as critical drivers of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), the second most common skin cancer in humans. Tumor-associated glial cells (TAGs) resemble embryonic Schwann cell lineage stages, are abundant in the stroma of premalignant lesions and established murine and human cSCC, and are essential for tumor formation. TAG activation in premalignant lesions is triggered by UV-induced anti-inflammatory macrophages, which in turn are polarized by TAGs into pro-tumorigenic FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, key components of the cSCC microenvironment. Consequently, TAG depletion reduces FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in keratinocytes, thereby impairing cSCC initiation by disrupting intercellular communication required for tumor development. As most solid tumors are innervated and harbor peripheral glia, our findings reveal TAGs as regulators of tumor initiation with potential relevance beyond skin cancer.

item.description:
Authors: Ryan T. Lingg, Shane B. Johnson, Dalton C. Hinz, Abdullahi A. Mohamed, Timothy D. Skog, Manuela Lizarazu, Sara A. Romig-Martin, Ryan T. LaLumiere, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Adaptive memory requires balancing generalization to avoid similar threats with discrimination to recognize safety. The prevailing view is that stress-induced increases in glucocorticoids underlie the enhancement of memory consolidation, strengthening memories and promoting their generalization—referred to here as the standard model. However, circuits that drive memory consolidation often also regulate glucocorticoid release, confounding whether their effects on memory are circuit-driven or hormonally mediated. Here we identify a prefrontal pathway that controls memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids. Using optogenetic manipulations in male rats, we found that post-training inhibition of the rostral prelimbic cortex (rPL) to anteroventral bed nuclei of the stria terminalis (avBST) pathway promoted contextual generalization in an inhibitory avoidance discrimination task without affecting memory strength. Although this manipulation further elevated corticosterone, it produced generalization even in adrenalectomized rats, demonstrating glucocorticoid independence. Conversely, post-training pathway excitation enhanced contextual discrimination. Recordings of calcium signals revealed context-specific engagement of both avBST and avBST-projecting rPL neurons during memory retrieval, with greater responses in the neutral than the aversive context. These findings reveal glucocorticoid-independent circuit control of memory specificity, setting boundary conditions on the standard model and demonstrating mechanistic heterogeneity that may inform stress-related disorders where memory generalization is a core feature.

item.description:
Authors: Cristina Colleoni, Leonardo Ormoli, Pierangela Gallina, Laura Rudilosso, Fabrizio Benedicenti, Martina Rocchi, Rossana Norata, Sara Degl’Innocenti, et al.
Journal: Nature Communications
Abstract: Abstract Senescence is a stress-induced program defined by permanent cell-cycle arrest and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Defective clearance of senescent cells promotes inflammation, tissue dysfunction, and ageing, yet determinants of their elimination remain poorly understood. Here, we model oncogene-induced senescence in the hematopoietic system by transplanting Braf V600E - or Braf ΔN -expressing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells into recipients with distinct immune backgrounds. Braf V600E induces a stronger senescence program and more aggressive disease than Braf ΔN . Survival depends on oncogene-expressing cell burden and host immunity: immunocompetent, lower-burden mice clear oncogene-expressing cells and survive long-term, whereas higher-burden mice show checkpoint upregulation, T-cell exhaustion, and early death. NSG, Rag1KO, and lymphocyte-depleted hosts fail to clear these cells, developing sustained inflammation and bone marrow failure. Rapamycin administration attenuates senescence-associated features and improves survival. These findings identify oncogenic intensity and adaptive immune competence as coupled determinants of senescent-cell fate, with implications for chronic inflammation and senescence-targeted therapies.
